title: Shape Analysis
notes: Open by reframing shape analysis as directional statistics after several quotient operations. The data begin as landmark coordinates, but the object of inference is not the drawing on the page. It is the configuration after translation, scale, and rotation have been treated as nuisance directions.

title: Lecture Route
notes: Use the route slide to keep the chapter from becoming a catalog of methods. Every stop removes or models a specific geometric feature: centering removes location, normalization removes size, phase quotienting removes planar rotation, Procrustes summaries compare shapes, tangent coordinates approximate local variation, and complex directional families provide global models.

title: Landmarks As Complex Data
notes: Establish the computational representation before any statistics appear. A planar landmark configuration is a complex vector, one entry per landmark. Similarity transformations move the entire vector in predictable ways, so the statistical task is to decide which parts of that movement are irrelevant to shape.

title: Helmert Preshape Pipeline
notes: Explain the pipeline as a sequence of invariant filters. Subtracting the centroid and multiplying by a Helmert submatrix both remove the all-ones translation direction, while division by norm removes scale. The resulting preshape lies on a complex unit sphere, where rotations still act as a common phase.

title: Phase Orbits Are Shapes
notes: Pause on the quotient because it is the conceptual hinge of the chapter. A preshape is one representative, but a shape is the entire circle of representatives obtained by common phase multiplication. Statistics on shape space must give the same answer anywhere along that orbit.

title: Procrustes Distance
notes: Introduce Procrustes distance through the modulus of the complex inner product. The phase of the inner product tells how to align one preshape to the other, but its absolute value tells how close the shapes are after the best alignment. This is why the formula is invariant under separate similarity transformations.

title: Procrustes Mean
notes: Describe the Procrustes mean as an averaging problem with alignment built in. Each observation is first rotated into the current frame, then the aligned representatives are averaged and renormalized. The mean is a shape class, so the displayed representative is only a convenient gauge.

title: Kendall Triangle Sphere
notes: Use triangle shapes as the place where the quotient becomes visible. For three landmarks, complex projective shape space is an ordinary sphere under the Hopf coordinates. Flat triangles sit on an equator, mirror images live on opposite sides, and common phase rotations leave the plotted point fixed.

title: Tangent Shape Coordinates
notes: Make the tangent approximation conditional rather than automatic. When shapes are concentrated near a Procrustes mean, aligned logarithmic residuals can be treated as horizontal tangent vectors. Horizontal means the vector changes shape rather than merely sliding along the phase orbit.

title: Shape PCA Modes
notes: Interpret tangent PCA as a local deformation tool. Principal components in the tangent space should describe interpretable changes in landmark geometry, not translations, rotations, or scale. The notebook sample deliberately hides nuisance transformations so the recovery of deformation modes becomes a check on the geometry.

title: Complex Directional Models
notes: Route model choice by sample space. Triangle shapes can be analyzed on the Kendall sphere, while general planar landmark shapes require phase-invariant models on complex projective space. Complex Bingham, Watson, and angular Gaussian families differ in how much anisotropy and robustness they allow.

title: Invariant Stress Test
notes: Turn the applied lab into an acceptance test. Raw coordinate gaps change dramatically under separate similarity transformations, but Procrustes shape distance stays fixed to numerical precision. That contrast is the reason the quotient geometry is not optional preprocessing.

title: Notebook Checks
notes: Use the check values as mathematical evidence. The Helmert matrix removes translation, preshapes have unit norm, Kendall coordinates stay on the sphere, tangent vectors are horizontal, and all named artifacts exist. These checks verify that the visuals and formulas refer to the same shape-space construction.

title: Common Failure Modes
notes: Warn against the shortcuts that make shape analysis look easier than it is. Comparing raw coordinate arrays confuses pose with shape, averaging unaligned preshapes blurs rotations, using tangent PCA globally ignores curvature, and fitting a directional model before naming the quotient can put density on the wrong space.

title: Analysis Workflow
notes: Present the workflow as an instructor-ready checklist. Start from the landmark registration convention, remove translation and scale, work with shape classes, choose Procrustes or tangent summaries according to concentration, then select complex directional models only when their symmetry matches the scientific question.

title: Takeaways
notes: Close by tying the chapter back to the course. Shape analysis is directional statistics on quotient sample spaces. The successful analysis is not the one with the most elaborate model, but the one whose summaries, approximations, and diagnostics respect the invariances of the measured shapes.
